title: Unified SDK credential lifecycle: API keys, rotation, and SSO token ergonomics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Define and implement consistent credential handling and rotation UX across Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go), plus guidance for enterprise SSO-based tokens and secret storage best practices. The work covers three areas: 1) runtime credential handling (env, file, keyring/keystore, cloud secret stores), 2) rotation and short-lived token flows (CLI + management endpoints + hot-reload in SDKs), and 3) streaming/retries ergonomics when auth changes mid-stream (reauth, reconnect, idempotency). We must provide code examples, end-to-end tests, and docs for engineers integrating Redwood SDKs in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) expose a single Auth abstraction that supports: static API keys, short-lived bearer tokens, and SSO-derived tokens
All SDKs can hot-reload credentials without restart (watch file or environment hooks documented and tested)
Rotation tooling: a CLI flow and REST endpoints documented for generating short-lived keys and performing rotation with zero-downtime best practices
Streaming clients gracefully handle 401/403 mid-stream by attempting token refresh once and reconnecting without duplicating client-visible output
Comprehensive docs and examples for: storing secrets (env vars, OS keyrings, cloud secret managers), implementing key rotation, and enterprise SSO token exchange
Security review completed and sign-off from Security team
Automated tests covering credential expiry, rotation scenarios, and streaming reauth paths in CI
work_notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SDK leads (Maya, Liam, Priya). Agreed to standardize on an AuthProvider interface across languages
2026-03-04: Prototype AuthProvider for Python that supports: EnvProvider, FileProvider (with watch), KeyringProvider, SecretManagerProvider (AWS/GCP/Azure)

2026-03-06: Design decision: use short-lived bearer tokens (default TTL 1h) issued by token service; long-lived API keys used only to mint short-lived tokens; recommend rotating long-lived keys quarterly

2026-03-08: Streaming behavior spec drafted: on 401, SDK should attempt token refresh once (if refresh provider available), then re-establish stream and continue; provide hooks to surface retry attempts to caller

2026-03-10: UX doc created for SSO exchange (OIDC code flow + client assertion) that enterprise customers will use to mint scoped tokens; included guidance for non-interactive server apps using SAML->OIDC bridge
2026-03-11: Security review request filed (SR-2026-14). Waiting for pen-test schedule. Implementing feature flags to toggle new auth flows in SDK CI builds
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-02): We need consistent env var names across languages. Proposal: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_TOKEN_PATH, REDWOOD_USE_KEYRING=true. Thoughts?
Priya Kumar (2026-03-03): +1 for single prefix. For enterprise SSO flows, include REDWOOD_SSO_CLIENT_ID and REDWOOD_SSO_PROVIDER to support multiple IdPs.
Liam O'Neill (2026-03-04): Implementation note: Python keyring will be optional dependency; fallback to file-based cache when not installed. We'll document tradeoffs in docs.
Security (Avery Park) (2026-03-05): Ensure SDK never logs full tokens or API keys. Add redaction helpers in logging layer. Also require token byte-length validation in all libs.

Maya Chen (2026-03-07): Decided to adopt the 'mint short-lived tokens from long-lived API keys' pattern. This reduces blast radius and simplifies rotation. We'll provide both flows for backwards compatibility.
Customer Success (Rafael Gomez) (2026-03-09): Several enterprise customers asked for SSO token refresh TTLs configurable by org. Add labels for tenant-specific TTLs in token service PRD.

Liam O'Neill (2026-03-12): PRs include example apps for each language. Requesting review from SDK leads and Security. Test matrix includes: env-var rotation, file update, keyring change, cloud secret update via webhook.
implementation_notes: AuthProvider interface sketch (all langs): get_token(context) -> token, refresh_token() optional, watch(callback) optional
Python: implement watch via watchdog to detect file changes; provide KeyringProvider using 'keyring' package; fallback order: Env -> File -> Keyring -> SecretManager
TypeScript: expose async function getToken() and provide browser and node implementations; in browser, only SSO/OIDC flows supported (no file or keyring)
Go: small footprint AuthProvider that reads from a JSON credential file with atomic writes; include sample integration with AWS Secrets Manager and HashiCorp Vault
Rotation: build 'rw-rotate' CLI that calls token-service/mint and updates a target secret location (file or secret manager); CLI supports --grace-period and --verify hooks
Streaming: add a small reconnect-backoff strategy that increments jittered backoff and preserves request idempotency for resumable streams; provide helper middleware for gRPC and websocket clients
Telemetry: emit anonymized auth events (auth_method, is_refresh, success/failure, latency) for debugging without logging tokens

Docs: include recommended patterns for local dev (env var + dev tokens), CI (use cloud secret manager), and production (short-lived tokens + secret manager). Provide migration guide from current SDK behavior
examples:
Python example: Use env var short-lived token with auto-refresh
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(auth_provider=EnvProvider('REDWOOD_TOKEN'))
# client automatically refreshes token when expired
